system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: GCP
G2: Azure
G3: Istio/Linkerd in production
G4: CKAD (expired)
G5: line management

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Listing Istio or service mesh because SRE ads ask for it
T2: Listing CKAD
T3: Claiming GCP/Azure for multi-cloud ads
T4: Claiming people management / Engineering Manager

# OUTPUT 1: CV
NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Site Reliability / Platform Engineer
nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior infrastructure engineer with 10 years of experience, including six running Kubernetes platforms
on AWS. Technical lead with hands-on experience designing, building and operating cloud
infrastructure, Terraform-based infrastructure as code, and self-service platforms for backend
developers. Delivered faster service deployment, lower infrastructure costs and more reliable
operations through observability, SLOs, capacity planning and incident management.
EXPERIENCE
Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS)
Apr 2022 - present
• Technical lead of a five-person platform team, operating an AWS EKS platform spanning eight
clusters, approximately 350 services and three regions.
• Built an internal developer platform with service templates, Argo CD GitOps and
Crossplane-based self-service provisioning for RDS, SQS and S3; reduced time from new service to
production from approximately two weeks to under one day.
• Introduced SLOs and error budgets for the 20 most critical services, reducing weekly on-call pages
by approximately 60%.
• Moved node provisioning to Karpenter with spot instances, reducing EC2 spend by 38%.
• Participated in the incident commander rotation and wrote the incident management and
post-mortem process.
Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games
Jan 2019 - Mar 2022
• Operated AWS infrastructure for game backends supporting titles with up to 1.2 million daily
active players, using EC2, ECS and subsequently EKS.
• Managed all AWS infrastructure through Terraform, with approximately 40 modules and Atlantis
for pull-request-based plan/apply workflows.
• Implemented Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki, replacing a noisy Nagios monitoring
setup.
• Performed pre-launch load testing with k6 and launch-day capacity planning.
Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting
Jul 2016 - Dec 2018
• Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration
management.
• Automated operational tasks with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer
incidents.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Cloud infrastructure: AWS, EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront
Infrastructure as code and delivery: Terraform, Atlantis, Crossplane, Argo CD, GitHub Actions,
Puppet
Containers and platforms: Kubernetes, Helm, Kustomize, Karpenter, Linux
Observability and reliability: Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, Loki, OpenTelemetry, SLOs, error
budgets, incident management, k6, capacity planning
Programming and automation: Go, Python, Bash
CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) - 2021, renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Professional - 2023
EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016
LANGUAGES
English (native), Urdu (conversational)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example
Corvale Mobility
Application: Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity
Dear Hiring Manager,
Corvale’s new train fleet needs cloud infrastructure that can move from initial design into
dependable production operation. I bring 10 years of infrastructure experience, including six
running Kubernetes platforms on AWS, alongside technical leadership, Terraform and
operational reliability expertise. This background is directly relevant to the cloud platform
and backend deployment foundations of your fleet-connectivity engagement.
As technical lead of Tallybrook’s five-person platform team, I operate an EKS platform
covering eight clusters, approximately 350 services and three regions. I built an internal
developer platform combining service templates, Argo CD GitOps and Crossplane-based
provisioning for RDS, SQS and S3, reducing the time from new service to production from
approximately two weeks to under one day. This work aligns with your need to take
infrastructure initiatives into production and help backend developers deploy services that are
straightforward to operate.
At Brightwater Games, I managed AWS infrastructure through approximately 40 Terraform
modules, using Atlantis for pull-request-based plan/apply workflows. I also implemented
Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki, and used k6 load testing to inform launch-day
capacity planning for game backends supporting titles with up to 1.2 million daily active
players. At Tallybrook, introducing SLOs and error budgets for 20 critical services reduced
weekly on-call pages by approximately 60%; I also wrote the incident and post-mortem
process. These are concrete foundations for the observability, alerting and reliability your
train-to-cloud services will require.
Your scope combines early architecture decisions with end-to-end operational ownership. My
experience building self-service infrastructure, leading a platform team and running
production services would support that work. I would welcome a discussion about how my
AWS, Terraform and reliability engineering experience could contribute to Corvale’s
fleet-connectivity platform.
Yours sincerely,
Nadia Brennan-Aziz

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
